## What's new in 1.5.0

**Four more Delrina releases: twenty in all, 429 modules.** All four ran on Delrina's Intermission, as Star Wars Screen Entertainment, The Far Side and Dilbert did, and one of them is Intermission itself.

| Release | Year | Modules |
|---|---|---|
| Opus 'n Bill Screen Saver | 1993 | 16 |
| Intermission 4.0 | 1993 | 54 |
| The Flintstones Screen Saver Collection | 1994 | 15 |
| Opus 'n Bill: On the Road Again! | 1994 | 16 |

The two Opus 'n Bill releases are animated scenes of Berkeley Breathed's Opus the penguin and Bill the Cat, and the Flintstones collection fifteen of Hanna-Barbera's Stone Age family. Intermission 4.0 is Delrina's screen saver itself, with modules of its own: graphic effects such as Fireworks, Ferns, Swarm and Tunnel, effects on your desktop's picture, a few animations, and three kinds of module Long After Dark had not run before, two FLI animations, a morph and a MultiSaver group, each played by its own Intermission player. Most of the new modules are animations played by Intermission's own animation player, which runs unchanged, and every one has a **Configure...** button that opens its original options.

**A Speed slider for Intermission 4.0's modules.** Intermission ran its modules as fast as the PC allowed, and most of Intermission 4.0's own move one small step each time they are called, so how fast they moved was how fast the PC was (the speed options a few of them have set only how big a step is). Those 36 modules, Dragon Kites, Ant Mine, Wriggly and Fireworks among them, have a **Speed** slider in their settings, which picks the pace of the emulated PC, module by module. **Normal** is our estimate of a typical PC of 1993, a 486 running Windows 3.1; **Slowest**, **Slow**, **Fast** and **Fastest** are about a quarter, half, twice and four times that pace, Fastest being the emulated PC at its full speed. Each slider starts where the module's motion is calm: most at Normal, Dragon Kites, Ping and Bricks at Slowest, Wriggly and Snow Flakes at Slow, and Space Shark, whose steps are heavy, at Fast. The setting is kept for each module, and the live preview shows a change as soon as you let go of the slider. The other 18, the animations among them, keep time by the clock, so they have none.

**Importing them.** The importer takes each one from your own copy, and can download it from the Internet Archive: the Opus 'n Bill Screen Saver as a 1993 bulletin-board copy of its three floppies, one ZIP per disk (select all three together), On the Road Again as a ZIP of its four floppies' files, Intermission 4.0 as a ZIP of its three floppy images, and the Flintstones from a 129.3 MB archive of a 1994 shareware collection, from which it takes only the release's three ZIPs. Two of them came in two builds, and either imports: the Opus 'n Bill Screen Saver's revised build of November 1993, with Censored Toasters in place of Death Toasters, and the Flintstones' May 1994 build, whose Prehistoric Vehicles is damaged in every copy online, so it imports without it. A ZIP or 7z whose files all sit in one folder is now read as that folder, and the notes bulletin boards left beside a release's files no longer stop an import. Every import is checked file by file against the original disks.

Nine of the new modules took the mouse under Intermission instead of ending (On the Road Again's The Butt Boys and Skating, and seven of the Flintstones'): like The Far Side's Pterodactyl, they run as ordinary screen savers, and input ends them. Intermission 4.0's Palette Animator shows only black on its own (it was made as the background of a MultiSaver group), and its Picture Show stays black until its **Configure...** names a folder of pictures. The Flintstones' DictaBird recorded from a microphone, which the emulated PC doesn't offer, so it shows only its own "Sound Support Not Available" line.

**Intermission 5.0** is not online as a product of its own: its engine came with On the Road Again and with Dilbert, both of which Long After Dark runs.

**Twenty covers.** The importer's window opens a little wider again, with seven covers to a row, so all twenty releases still show at once. Its **Download from the Internet Archive** page no longer grows to the height of the screen: it shows nine releases at a time and scrolls the rest, so it is about as tall as the page that leads to it.
